questionText:
The following relation records the age of 500 employees of a company, where $empNo$ (indicating the employee number) is the key:

$$empAge(\underline{empNo}, age)$$

Consider the following relational algebra expression:

$$\Pi_{empNo}(empAge \bowtie_{(age > age1)} \rho_{empNo1, age1}(empAge))$$

What does the above expression generate?
options: Employee numbers of only those employees whose age is the maximum.
Employee numbers of only those employees whose age is more than the age of exactly one other employee.
Employee numbers of all employees whose age is not the minimum.
Employee numbers of all employees whose age is the minimum.
explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the Renaming Operation
The expression $\rho_{empNo1, age1}(empAge)$ renames the relation $empAge$ to have attributes $empNo1$ and $age1$.

Step 2: Analyze the Theta Join
The operation $empAge \bowtie_{(age > age1)} \rho_{empNo1, age1}(empAge)$ performs a Theta Join between $empAge$ and its renamed copy on the condition $age > age1$. This pairs each employee with all employees who have a strictly smaller age.

Step 3: Analyze the Projection
The projection $\Pi_{empNo}(...)$ extracts the $empNo$ of employees who satisfy the condition $age > age1$. An employee $empNo$ will be present in this result if and only if there exists at least one employee in the company who is younger than them.

Step 4: Conclusion
The only employees excluded from the result are those who do not have any employee younger than them, i.e., those who have the minimum age.

Therefore, the expression returns the employee numbers of all employees whose age is not the minimum.

Hence, option (C) is correct.
